95217833.title: Lucky_Day_(Doctor_Who)
95217833.extract:
# Lucky Day (Doctor Who)

Lucky Day is the fourth episode of the 2025 season of the British television series Doctor Who, marketed globally as Season 2 and referred to by UK press as Series 15. Written by Pete McTighe and directed by Peter Hoar, the episode first released in the United Kingdom on BBC iPlayer on 3 May 2025 at 08:00 BST, followed by a same‑day broadcast on BBC One at 19:10. Outside the UK, new episodes of the season were made available weekly on Disney+ according to local availability and platform release schedules. The story focuses on Ruby Sunday’s life back on Earth without the Doctor, as UNIT helps protect her new boyfriend Conrad from a terrifying new threat called the Shreek. The episode runs 46 minutes and features Ncuti Gatwa as the Doctor, Millie Gibson as Ruby Sunday, and Jonah Hauer‑King as Conrad, with returning UNIT characters led by Jemma Redgrave’s Kate Lethbridge‑Stewart. Seven‑day consolidated UK viewing figures reported by Radio Times (from BARB data) totalled 2.802 million. Contemporary reviews and commentaries from mainstream outlets described the episode’s themes of fandom, conspiracy, and the Doctor’s darker side, while noting its “Doctor‑light” perspective that centres Ruby’s arc. 

## Scope, status, and title

- Medium and status: Lucky Day is a televised episode in Doctor Who’s 2025 run on BBC One and BBC iPlayer in the UK, and distributed internationally by Disney+. It is part of the ongoing television series produced by BBC Studios. 
- Series placement and era: It is episode four of the 2025 season featuring Ncuti Gatwa as the Fifteenth Doctor and Millie Gibson as companion Ruby Sunday, situated between The Well and The Story and the Engine. UK press frequently refers to the 2025 run as Series 15, while official BBC and Disney+ materials style the season as Season 2. 
- Title and styling: The episode’s official title is Lucky Day, as used on BBC iPlayer, the BBC Media Centre mediapack, and the Disney+ Press media kit. 

## Plot

Ruby Sunday has returned to life on Earth without the Doctor, struggling to adjust while joining forces with UNIT to confront a new alien entity, the Shreek. Ruby embarks on a relationship with Conrad Clark, a podcaster whose work partly tracks sightings of the Doctor. As Conrad becomes targeted by the Shreek, Ruby and UNIT attempt to protect him, uncovering layers of conspiracy and misinformation that complicate their efforts. The Doctor appears “out of order” relative to Ruby’s timeline, confronting Conrad directly and making comments that steer the Doctor toward future investigative steps, including the name Belinda Chandra. The episode frames the Shreek threat amid human dynamics around deception and online conspiracies, with Ruby navigating trauma from her travels with the Doctor while UNIT coordinates a high‑risk response. 

## Cast and characters

Principal and notable cast as credited on official BBC pages include: 
- Ncuti Gatwa as the Doctor 
- Millie Gibson as Ruby Sunday 
- Jonah Hauer‑King as Conrad Clark 
- Varada Sethu as Belinda Chandra 
- Jemma Redgrave as Kate Lethbridge‑Stewart 
- Ruth Madeley as Shirley Bingham 
- Michelle Greenidge as Carla Sunday 
- Angela Wynter as Cherry Sunday 
- Anita Dobson as Mrs Flood 
- Gethin Alderman as the Shreek 
- Aidan Cook as the Vlinx 
- Nicholas Briggs as Voice of the Vlinx 
- Cameos as themselves: Reeta Chakrabarti, Joel Dommett, Alex Jones 

## Production credits

- Writer: Pete McTighe 
- Director: Peter Hoar 
- Producer: Vicki Delow 
- Executive producers: Russell T Davies, Julie Gardner, Jane Tranter, Joel Collins, Phil Collinson 
- Music: Murray Gold (series credit) 

## Development and production

The BBC Media Centre mediapack frames Lucky Day as Ruby’s story in the aftermath of life with the Doctor, exploring what happens when the Doctor is absent and how that heightens jeopardy for human characters. McTighe highlighted the episode’s focus on Ruby and on a “savage” new monster, the Shreek, that “cannot be reasoned with.” Director Peter Hoar described leaning into gothic horror in at least one scene, while Millie Gibson spoke about Ruby opening up to Conrad about PTSD from her travels with the Doctor; Jonah Hauer‑King characterised Conrad as a “superfan” running a podcast that, in part, follows Doctor sightings. 

McTighe has also discussed the episode’s place in his wider work on the franchise, noting that after handing in his first draft of Lucky Day he was invited by showrunner Russell T Davies to collaborate further, subsequently writing for the spin‑off The War Between the Land and the Sea. 

## Continuity and placement

- Episode order: Lucky Day follows The Well and precedes The Story and the Engine in the 2025 season. 
- UNIT and returning elements: The episode features UNIT’s modern incarnation led by Kate Lethbridge‑Stewart, with Shirley Bingham among returning characters. 
- Narrative timing and arcs: Radio Times’ continuity coverage details that the Doctor confronts Conrad earlier in the Doctor’s personal timeline, with dialogue including the line “Have you met Belinda Chandra yet?”, thereby connecting the episode to broader season arcs involving Belinda. 

## Release and distribution

- United Kingdom: New episodes in the 2025 season were released weekly on BBC iPlayer at 08:00 on Saturdays, with Lucky Day arriving on 3 May 2025. The BBC One broadcast followed that evening at 19:10, as listed in BBC schedules. 
- International: Disney+ carried the season outside the UK, premiering Season 2 on 12 April 2025 at 00:00 PT (03:00 ET) with weekly releases thereafter. Lucky Day formed part of that global rollout schedule. 

## Accessibility, companion content, and marketing

- Accessibility: BBC iPlayer provides Signed and Audio Described versions of Lucky Day. 
- Companion programme: A behind‑the‑scenes episode of Doctor Who: Unleashed corresponding to Lucky Day (28 minutes) was released on BBC iPlayer and broadcast on BBC Three and BBC One. 
- BBC promotional materials: The BBC Programmes site hosts a short behind‑the‑scenes clip featuring Millie Gibson and Jonah Hauer‑King discussing the episode. 
- Disney+ Press media kit: Episodic images labelled “Lucky Day” are available in the official media kit, confirming title styling in global marketing. 
- Costume note: Millie Gibson discussed a late‑episode outfit that subtly nods to David Tennant’s era, crediting costume designer Pam Downe’s approach to visual storytelling for character progression. 

## Audience metrics

Radio Times, citing BARB seven‑day consolidated data, reported Lucky Day at 2.802 million UK viewers, noting this figure among the season’s lower consolidated totals to that point. Episodes in the 2025 run were made available at 08:00 on BBC iPlayer prior to the same‑day BBC One broadcast, which can affect overnight figures relative to consolidated performance. 

## Critical reception

- The Guardian’s recap characterised the episode as timely, with Ruby taking centre stage against internet conspiracy theorists, and highlighted contemporary resonances in its themes. 
- Den of Geek’s review discussed strengths and weaknesses of the “Doctor‑light” framing and the episode’s engagement with fandom and misinformation, offering a mixed appraisal while noting performances. 
- Radio Times published multiple commentaries: one article argued the episode demonstrated why the Doctor cannot lose his dark side, quoting an uncompromising confrontation with Conrad; another piece criticised the lack of an on‑screen moment of present‑day support between the Doctor and Ruby, framing it as a missed emotional beat for the pair’s relationship. 

## Notability

Lucky Day is covered by official BBC programme pages and press materials, widely listed in broadcast schedules, and discussed in mainstream entertainment publications and national press. The episode’s development comments (from writer, director, and cast), companion content, broadcast data reported via Radio Times from BARB, and multiple independent reviews together provide sufficient reliable sourcing for a comprehensive, neutral article.

Doctor Who season 2 arrives on BBC and Disney+ on April 12 2025 with Alan Cumming to guest star
===============================================================================================

Cumming will guest star in the second episode as Mr Ring-a-Ding

Published: 02:00 pm, 26 February 2025

![Image 5: Left: A man in a long coat stands with his back to the camera, holding a sonic device against the backdrop of space. Left: A tall, thin blue cartoon character emerges from between a pair of red velvet curtains, wearing a purple suit and smiling](https://ichef.bbci.co.uk/images/ic/400xn/p0ktq81h.jpg)

It’s time to set your alarms! The Doctor (Ncuti Gatwa) is on his way back to your screens, this time with a new addition to the TARDIS, Belinda Chandra (Varada Sethu).

Season two will officially launch on Saturday 12 April at 8am on BBC iPlayer and later that day on BBC One in the UK. At the same time, those outside of the UK can watch the Doctor and Belinda on their epic adventures on Disney+ where available.

And that’s not all… Emmy Award winner Alan Cumming will guest star in the second episode as Mr Ring-a-Ding. He’s a happy, funny, singalong cartoon, who lives in Sunny Town with his friend Sunshine Sally. However, in 1952, after years of repeats in cinemas across the land, Mr Ring-a-Ding suddenly looks beyond the screen and sees the real world outside - and the consequences are terrifying.

![Image 6: A tall, slim powder blue coloured cartoon character emerges from a pair of red velvet curtains wearing a purple suit with yellow waistcoat and pink bow tie, smiling.](https://ichef.bbci.co.uk/images/ic/400xn/p0ktq8b6.jpg)

Russell T Davies, Showrunner says: “Only Alan Cumming could give a runaway cartoon so much wit, malice, danger and fun. He makes the whole universe of Doctor Who wilder and madder than ever, and it’s an absolute honour to welcome him on board the TARDIS.”

![Image 7: Left: A figure in a long coat stands with his their back to the camera against the backdrop of space. Right: A woman in a denim outfit stares worriedly at something off screen against a backdrop of space. Doctor Who 12th April is written in pastel pink and green lettering](https://ichef.bbci.co.uk/images/ic/400xn/p0ktq9bt.jpg)

The new season stars Ncuti Gatwa as the Doctor, Varada Sethu as Belinda Chandra, and Millie Gibson as Ruby Sunday. Also adventuring through time and space this season are Rose Ayling-Ellis, Anita Dobson, Christopher Chung, Michelle Greenidge, Jonah Hauer-King, Ruth Madeley, Jemma Redgrave, and Susan Twist.

Doctor Who is produced by Bad Wolf with BBC Studios for the BBC and Disney Branded Television.

*   **[Watch Doctor Who on BBC iPlayer and add to your Watchlist now](https://www.bbc.co.uk/iplayer/group/m001rzf7)**

2.title: Doctor Who Lucky Day cast and creatives on Ruby's return, romance with Jonah-Hauer King's Conrad and a terrifying new monster in "edge of your seat" episode
2.description: UNIT are back and facing a deadly new threat - The Shreek!
2.content:
Published: 08:00 pm, 28 April 2025

Doctor Who season 2 episode 4 sees Ruby Sunday facing life back on earth without the Doctor.

But when a dangerous new threat emerges, can Ruby and UNIT save her new boyfriend, Conrad, from the terrifying Shreek?

We caught up with the cast and creatives to find out all about Lucky Day...

*   **[Watch Doctor Who on BBC iPlayer and add to your Watchlist](https://www.bbc.co.uk/iplayer/episodes/p0gglvqn/doctor-who)**

**Millie Gibson (Ruby Sunday)**
-------------------------------

![Image 1: Two women look out a window, shocked or frightened by what they see](https://ichef.bbci.co.uk/images/ic/400xn/p0l70v01.jpg)

(Image: BBC Studios/Bad Wolf/Lara Cornell)

**How does it feel to be back in the Whoniverse?**

It feels like returning home after a long day. It's so nice to be back playing Ruby Sunday in a whole new light. As Ruby grows up, so do I. In season two, you see more of a mature and stronger version of Ruby. She’s recovering from her season one adventures, and you see her learn to deal with that a bit. I'm really excited to be back, it was a fun few episodes to read for Ruby.

**What can you tell us about Ruby, and what she’s been up to since we last saw her?**

You saw her look out the window in [Joy to The World](https://www.bbc.co.uk/iplayer/episode/m0026d24/doctor-who-joy-to-the-world) written by Steven Moffat, and I think she is waiting for the Doctor. She's waiting for an adventure, but she's also getting back to her life with her family, her new dad, her new mum, and Carla and her Gran. It’s still as bonkers as ever in the Sunday household! [Laughs].

Ruby is going back to her life and pretending everything's back to normal, but she can't really get her head around all the things she saw while travelling with the Doctor. So, she's just waiting around and trying to process all of that.

**What can audiences expect from this episode?**

UNIT are back, and Ruby gets her chance to shine with UNIT, which is lovely, because I absolutely love working with Jemma Redgrave and our beautiful Ruth Madeley. Honestly, those two women are just incredible to work with. They’re like Ruby's third and fourth mothers. There is even a line in the episode where Ruth's character, Shirley, makes a joke about it. So, UNIT are back, and we are uncovering a new monster called the Shreek, and that is the big creature in the episode. It’s a fabulous episode!

**Is there anything you can tease about Conrad, played by Jonah Hauer-King?**

Oh My God, I absolutely love Jonah! He was just a burst of energy. It’s not every day you get told your boyfriend is going to be played by Prince Eric [laughs]. I was really, really chuffed. He is such a professional, and he's such a giving actor. I know a lot of people say that, but I really mean it with Jonah.

I’m excited for people to see what’s in store for Ruby’s first love interest. Jonah plays him exceptionally and I couldn't imagine anyone else playing him.

![Image 2: Two people sit across from each other at a high table in a bar, holding hands across the table and looking lovingly at each other](https://ichef.bbci.co.uk/images/ic/400xn/p0l70v1g.jpg)

(Image: BBC Studios/Bad Wolf/James Pardon)

**What is the dynamic like between Ruby and Conrad?**

I think he gives off the energy that he wants to match to the Doctor. It’s one of them where your new boyfriend wants to be better than your ex, however he is just so sweet and so clumsy. He has these really cute characteristics and attributes where he's just a little bit of a clown, and it's a lovable energy.

Ruby loves being able to talk about her adventures with someone that is genuinely interested. She doesn’t feel like a strange outsider in her own world anymore, which is a really beautiful thing.

**Do you have any standout memories from set filming this episode?**

Oh, so many, so many. I love working with Peter Hoar. He was such a cool director, and he gave me so much new light into Ruby’s character. He really wanted to explore this new side to the companion. You rarely see the companion after the events because they either die or you just don't see them again.

There's a scene where Ruby talks about all her experiences in season one, and I love a specific line that Pete McTighe wrote for Ruby. She's opening up to Conrad about her PTSD from her travels with the Doctor. It was a really strong speech that was also kind of humorous, because it's so bonkers what she’s experienced.

Ruby is going back to this normal life after traveling the universe. It’s a really cool concept, because how does someone deal with that?

**What was it like acting alongside the monster The Shreek in this episode?**

Gethin Alderman who played The Shreek was the loveliest person ever, but terrifying. There is a scene in a cafe where Ruby is telling Conrad about The Shreek. Peter Hoar does a really cool kind of nightmare story where what she’s telling him actually happens. It's all kind of melted into one another to make this horror story aspect come to life. Gethin was honestly terrifying and we were scared for our lives [laughs], but he played it so well.

**This episode reunites Ruby with UNIT, along with Ruth Madeley who returns in this episode. How was it working with her?**

I had never worked with Ruth before so that was really exciting. As the season goes on, you see Ruby's and Shirley's relationship develop a lot more. And yes, she's her third mother. I feel like her and Ruby have a northern sense of humour that they can relate with. Ruth lives in Manchester, so when we met, we were like, ‘Oh, you've been to this pub’, so that was always great! It was a breath of fresh air working with Ruth and developing that relationship with Shirley.

![Image 3: The Doctor stands opposite Ruby Sunday, holding a small vial of something](https://ichef.bbci.co.uk/images/ic/400xn/p0l70vdm.jpg)

(Image: BBC Studios/Bad Wolf/James Pardon)

**Ruby has a signature style, what will we see her wearing in this season?**

It's a bit more grown up, but it's still cool. She's kind of packed away the tweed vibes, I'd say.

My favourite outfit is towards the end of the episode, I genuinely thought they dressed me like David Tennant! [Laughs]. I had a pinstripe waistcoat and pinstripe pants and then a white shirt, I was literally just like David Tennant.

Pam Downe, our costume designer, has a really subtle way of illustrating that these are what these characters would wear when they get older. The colour scheme is a lot of plums, a lot of dark greens and a lot of dark blues, it's just more mature colours.

**If you could travel in the TARDIS to any time and place in the universe, where would you go and why?**

The 1800s. I love the corsets and the costumes. And we should bring balls back. They should be a thing like the episode Rogue in season one. I was just living my dream filming that. So, yeah, I think somewhere with the era of ball gowns and big party events and people courting one another.

**If you had to describe the episode in one word or phrase, what would it be?**

Haunting and revealing…

Jonah Hauer-King (Conrad)
-------------------------

![Image 4: A man stands outside the TARDIS in an alleyway looking nervous](https://ichef.bbci.co.uk/images/ic/400xn/p0l70v4c.jpg)

(Image: BBC Studios/Bad Wolf/James Pardon)

**How does it feel to be joining the Whoniverse?**

It feels amazing. It’s a very, very iconic TV show that’s been on our screens for decades. I feel like it’s a big honour because it’s sort of a rite of passage. I went to the screening for the first episode, and at the beginning they did a showreel of Doctor Who over the last twenty years. Not only did it include the iconic Doctors and companions we’ve had, but it was also a reminder of how many incredible actors have popped up over the years in roles and big and small. There’s been so many incredible actors in the show, and it feels like a massive privilege to now be part of that universe.

**How did the role come about?**

I had an email from my agent saying that Russell (T Davies) had been in touch to ask if I was interested in doing it. The answer was yes, so he sent me a script to look at. I read it and it felt really exciting.

It has a lot of what we have come to expect from Doctor Who with the heart and the soul and the monsters and the scares. But, I think there’s something particularly grounded and unique about this episode. I really liked it and told him I would love to do it. I’ve been a big fan of Russell’s work in and outside of Doctor Who, so any chance to work with him was very appealing. It was great that it happened to be on Doctor Who.

**Were you a fan of the show before you joined?**

Yes, I was a fan of the show, but in a way that I think lots of people are. It’s so present in our minds, certainly for the British audience and I’m sure that extends all around the world. It’s so part of our TV history and our popular culture. It’s so immersed in our consciousness.

**This episode sees the return of Ruby Sunday, how was it working with Millie Gibson?**

Millie is fantastic. I hadn’t seen her work in Doctor Who when I did this episode as the show hadn’t come out yet, but I was immediately struck by her talent and warmth. We had such a giggle on set.

Without giving too much away, the episode is very much about their dynamic and relationship. We were on set together all day every day for a few weeks. We got on so well and had so much fun working together and being in Cardiff. When her episodes came out for the first season, it was such a joy to watch her, because I saw the character that she had been bringing to life before my eyes.

**How was it to be on the Doctor Who set and see the scale of the show?**

The sets are very unique, they have amazing scale. Doctor Who prides itself on doing things practically as much as they can. They built so much of it. They found some fantastic locations and built some amazing things at the studios in Cardiff. It’s just really fun to see, and it does help you as an actor because everything is there, and it’s tactile. It’s right in front of you. You can just be present, there’s less imagination needed, it’s all right in front of you. Your surroundings really inform your performance, so having the sets there is a great help.

![Image 5: Two people smile at each other as they kneel on a floor where a series of papers have fallen](https://ichef.bbci.co.uk/images/ic/400xn/p0l70wdl.jpg)

(Image: BBC Studios/Bad Wolf/James Pardon)

**Is there anything you can tell us about your character Conrad?**

Conrad meets the Doctor when he is a young boy. From that point, he’s obsessed with him. He’s desperate to meet him and idolises him on some level. He’s dedicated a lot of his life to finding out about him and trying to meet him. When we meet Conrad, he’s running a podcast which at least in part, focusses on sightings of the Doctor. He’s a superfan.

**Do you have a highlight from your experience on the show?**

There are quite a few. Working with Millie was brilliant, and working with Peter Hoar, our director. I also had a fantastic scene with Ncuti. It was the first time that we had really worked together with this really long brilliant scene written by Pete McTighe. It was cool to see Ncuti work in the flesh. He’s every bit as charismatic as you would imagine and he has this amazing energy. It was a really well written duologue between the two of them.

**What can viewers expect from the episode?**

There’s a lot in it. It has everything you want. It has monsters, it has twists, it has scares, it has love, romance, a bit of friendship, a bit of good vs evil, it’s the whole shebang.

**If you could travel anywhere in time and space, where would you go?**

I know it’s an obvious one, but I would quite like to see the dinosaurs. I’d like to see what the world looked like, I bet it was ridiculously beautiful. I don’t think I’d last more than an hour at best, but if I had the TARDIS to make a quick exit before getting eaten, I’d love to see the dinosaurs in all their magnificence.

**Can you sum up your episode in one word or phrase?**

Edge of your seat.

Pete McTighe (Writer)
---------------------

![Image 6: A woman in a denim jacket stands looking at something over her shoulder at night. She looks shocked and distressed.](https://ichef.bbci.co.uk/images/ic/400xn/p0kvn4z3.jpg)

(BBC Studios)

**Welcome back to the Whoniverse! What is it like writing for Doctor Who?**

Doctor Who is the reason I'm a writer, the reason I work in TV. It's my favourite thing in the world. So, it feels like coming home. This was *my* lucky day! Working with Russell T Davies and the Bad Wolf team is always such a brilliant experience. I've created and showrun my own shows and written hundreds of hours of TV, but nothing beats Doctor Who - I've literally had the best couple of years of my career, working with Russell on [Tales of the TARDIS](https://www.bbc.co.uk/iplayer/episodes/p0gmj4tn/tales-of-the-tardis), Lucky Day and [The War Between The Land And The Sea](https://www.bbc.com/mediacentre/2024/the-war-between-the-land-and-the-sea-doctor-who-spin-off). It's been a total joy.

**What can you tell us about this episode?**

What I loved about writing this episode was being able to explore what happens when the Doctor isn't around, when he's off saving other planets. Instantly, without the Doctor, there's more jeopardy for the human characters, the stakes are higher, and they're pushed to places they wouldn't necessarily have to go if he was there to save the day. Of course, the Doctor *is* in the episode, in a very significant way, but really Lucky Day is Ruby's story. I love what Millie Gibson did in her first season, so being able to come in and develop her character even further was really exciting.

Throughout all of Doctor Who – with the exception of Sarah-Jane Smith - we've never really explored what happens to someone after they stop travelling with the Doctor, and how those adventures impacted them. I loved being able to delve into that aspect of the character. I also enjoyed developing Jonah Hauer-King's character, Conrad, Ruby's new boyfriend. He's someone who adores Ruby and wants to be as brave and heroic as the Doctor, but in doing so he puts himself and Ruby in terrible danger.

![Image 7: Ruby, Kate and Shirley are in UNIT HQ, looking shocked at something off screen. Colonel Ibrahim stands with his gun poised.](https://ichef.bbci.co.uk/images/ic/400xn/p0kf2tsc.jpg)

We've got a great new monster in this episode as well, it's savage and terrifying and cannot be reasoned with. It was also a massive treat to be able to write for UNIT; for Kate, Shirley and Colonel Ibrahim, who swoop in to help Ruby and Conrad from the horrors that have been unleashed. Oh, for classic series fans we also have Paul Jericho in the episode - he played The Castellan, an officious, shady Time Lord during Peter Davison's era. He's playing a new character now, publican Alfie. Or is he? Maybe the Castellan wasn't killed in 'The Five Doctors' (1983), escaped the destruction of Gallifrey and ended up running a pub in an English village? Much better, let's go with that.

**If you could travel in the TARDIS to any time and place in the universe, where would you go?**

I would park myself on a comfy sofa in cold November 1963, and spend the next six years watching (and recording, to share with you guys) all the missing episodes of Doctor Who!

**If you had to describe the episode in one word or phrase, what would it be?**

Thrilling. Which is a good word for this whole season actually.

Peter Hoar (Director)
---------------------

![Image 8: A man stands in the middle of a room full of mannequins or statues covered by large white sheets looking concerned](https://ichef.bbci.co.uk/images/ic/400xn/p0l70wy1.jpg)

(Image: BBC Studios/Bad Wolf/James Pardon)

**You directed an episode of Doctor Who in 2011. What was it like to return?**

It was fantastic. I had my good friends around me and a very positive, exciting new world to discover. I have also changed as a director, and I felt so much more confident. But my love for the show has never diminished.

**What can audiences expect from this episode?**

The episode is quite a journey from its unassuming beginning to high octane sci-fi thrill ride. We had many references for this episode from all kinds of cinema and TV including Devils End from The Daemons to Aliens.

**This episode has lots of familiar faces including the UNIT team. What was it like working with them?**

It was a joy! They are all superb without question. Watching them face such an extreme foe as this, then working as a team, being pushed to the edge, seeing their humanity tested to its limits… I hope will make a great episode. The cast worked so hard to bring this to life and deserve huge praise. I particularly like one shot where the three women of UNIT stand shoulder to shoulder.

**This episode sees the return of Ruby Sunday (Millie Gibson), and Jonah Hauer-King joins the cast as Conrad, what can you tease about the dynamic between the pair?**

Jonah and Millie were a great duo. Jonah fitted so smoothly into the family, and it was exciting to watch a new fresh dynamic emerge. Ruby needs a new hero and Conrad thinks he’s all that, but we discover quickly that it’s Ruby who’s better in a dangerous situation…

![Image 9: Left: A woman stands looking defiantly at something off screen while a man behind her points a gun in the same direction. Right: A woman sits at a keyboard looking concerned at what's happening behind her off screen](https://ichef.bbci.co.uk/images/ic/400xn/p0l70xg9.jpg)

(Images: BBC Studios/Bad Wolf/James Pardon)

**We know that this episode takes us back to the UNIT Tower. What is it like being on that set?**

It’s a huge place with a lot of visual promise. It led me to make a new pitch for the end sequence that we had a lot of fun shooting. We threw everything at them. Literally

**There is a terrifying monster in this episode, what was it like bringing it to life on camera?**

Would it be Doctor Who without a monster? This one is genuinely scary. And we leant right in to it - one scene in particular we went full gothic horror.

**If you could travel in the TARDIS to any time and place in the universe, where would you go?**

The distant future as far away as possible

**How would you sum up this episode?**

Scary, surprising and romantic.

Doctor Who writer on why new episode Lucky Day is reminiscent of Sarah Jane Smith
=================================================================================

Pete McTighe has said that Sarah Jane marks the exception to a rule – until now.

![Image 4: Elisabeth Sladen as Sarah Jane Smith with K9 in Doctor Who](https://images.immediate.co.uk/production/volatile/sites/3/2022/10/doctor-who-elisabeth-sladen-sarah-jane-6fc5e22.jpg?quality=90&resize=980,654)

BBC/Adrian Rogers

*   [James Hibbs](https://www.radiotimes.com/author/jameshibbs/)

Published: Tuesday, 29 April 2025 at 8:00 am

[Subscribe to Radio Times – 5 weeks for £2](https://www.buysubscriptions.com/print/radio-times-magazine-subscription?promo=RT542TPBS1&utm_medium=Brandsite&utm_source=radiotimes.com&utm_campaign=RTAug25_RT542TPBS1&utm_content=promotional-link&style=brand)

*   [Share on pinterest](https://www.pinterest.com/pin/create/button/?url=https://www.radiotimes.com/tv/sci-fi/doctor-who-lucky-day-sarah-jane-newsupdate/&media=https://images.immediate.co.uk/production/volatile/sites/3/2022/10/doctor-who-elisabeth-sladen-sarah-jane-6fc5e22.jpg&description=Doctor%20Who%20writer%20on%20why%20new%20episode%20Lucky%20Day%20is%20reminiscent%20of%20Sarah%20Jane%20Smith)
*   [Share on reddit](https://www.reddit.com/submit?url=https://www.radiotimes.com/tv/sci-fi/doctor-who-lucky-day-sarah-jane-newsupdate/&title=Doctor%20Who%20writer%20on%20why%20new%20episode%20Lucky%20Day%20is%20reminiscent%20of%20Sarah%20Jane%20Smith)
*   [Email to a friend](mailto:?subject=On%20RadioTimes%20today:&body=I%20saw%20this%20and%20thought%20it%20might%20interest%20you...%0A%0Ahttps://www.radiotimes.com/tv/sci-fi/doctor-who-lucky-day-sarah-jane-newsupdate/)

The next episode of [Doctor Who](https://www.radiotimes.com/tv/sci-fi/doctor-who-season-15-release-date/), titled [Lucky Day](https://www.radiotimes.com/tv/sci-fi/doctor-who-ruby-ptsd-episode-newsupdate/), comes from writer Pete McTighe, who has previously been behind the episodes Kerblam! and Praxeus, and it picks up with Millie Gibson's Ruby Sunday.

Ad

Ruby notably left the TARDIS at the end of season 14, in order to spend more time getting to know her newly-found birth mother. Now, the series is set to show how her life has continued on since she parted ways with the Doctor.

Speaking recently, McTighe has noted that this is a rarity for the series, but picked up on one character for whom that experience was explored in depth - Elisabeth Sladen's Sarah Jane Smith.

McTighe said: "What I loved about writing this episode was being able to explore what happens when the Doctor isn't around, when he's off saving other planets.

"Instantly, without the Doctor, there's more jeopardy for the human characters, the stakes are higher, and they're pushed to places they wouldn't necessarily have to go if he was there to save the day.

"Of course, the Doctor *is* in the episode, in a very significant way, but really Lucky Day is Ruby's story. I love what Millie Gibson did in her first season, so being able to come in and develop her character even further was really exciting.

"Throughout all of Doctor Who – with the exception of Sarah Jane Smith - we've never really explored what happens to someone after they stop travelling with the Doctor, and how those adventures impacted them. I loved being able to delve into that aspect of the character."

![Image 5: Millie Gibson as Ruby Sunday in Doctor Who looking concerned at night](https://images.immediate.co.uk/production/volatile/sites/3/2025/04/513180-297eb54.jpg?quality=90&fit=700,467)

Millie Gibson as Ruby Sunday in Doctor Who.BBC Studios/Bad Wolf/Lara Cornell

McTighe continued: "I also enjoyed developing Jonah Hauer-King's character, Conrad, Ruby's new boyfriend. He's someone who adores Ruby and wants to be as brave and heroic as the Doctor, but in doing so he puts himself and Ruby in terrible danger.

**Read more:**

*   [Black Mirror creator Charlie Brooker was asked to write for Doctor Who](https://www.radiotimes.com/movies/scifi/black-mirror-charlie-brooker-write-doctor-who-newsupdate/)
*   [Doctor Who guest star previously auditioned for a Peter Capaldi episode](https://www.radiotimes.com/tv/sci-fi/christopher-chung-doctor-who-peter-capaldi-newsupdate/)

"We've got a great new monster in this episode as well, it's savage and terrifying and cannot be reasoned with. It was also a massive treat to be able to write for UNIT; for Kate, Shirley and Colonel Ibrahim, who swoop in to help Ruby and Conrad from the horrors that have been unleashed.

"Oh, for classic series fans we also have Paul Jericho in the episode - he played the Castellan, an officious, shady Time Lord during Peter Davison's era. He's playing a new character now, publican Alfie. Or is he?

"Maybe the Castellan wasn't killed in The Five Doctors (1983), escaped the destruction of Gallifrey and ended up running a pub in an English village? Much better, let's go with that."

While the show has checked in on some previous companions in the past, such as Freema Agyeman's Martha Jones in season 4, Sarah Jane is no doubt the character to whom this is most applicable - after all, she got an entire spin-off show, [The Sarah Jane Adventures](https://www.radiotimes.com/tv/sci-fi/doctor-who-whoniverse-in-order/), after returning in season 2's School Reunion.

McTighe himself is currently behind an upcoming spin-off for the series, [The War Between the Land and the Sea](https://www.radiotimes.com/tv/sci-fi/war-between-land-and-sea-release-doctor-who/), which he has co-written with Doctor Who showrunner Russell T Davies.

Doctor Who confirms 7-day ratings for The Story and the Engine
==============================================================

The episode has returned the lowest 7-day ratings from season 15.

![Image 4: Varada Sethu as Belinda Chandra and Ncuti Gatwa as The Doctor in Doctor Who, stood outside the TARDIS](https://images.immediate.co.uk/production/volatile/sites/3/2025/05/519192-1-84894ed-e1746713254820.jpg?quality=90&resize=980,654)

BBC Studios/Bad Wolf/Dan Fearon

*   [Ned Holmes](https://www.radiotimes.com/author/nedholmes/)

Published: Tuesday, 20 May 2025 at 12:45 pm

[Subscribe to Radio Times – 5 weeks for £2](https://www.buysubscriptions.com/print/radio-times-magazine-subscription?promo=RT542TPBS1&utm_medium=Brandsite&utm_source=radiotimes.com&utm_campaign=RTAug25_RT542TPBS1&utm_content=promotional-link&style=brand)
*   [Share on facebook](https://www.facebook.com/sharer.php?u=https://www.radiotimes.com/tv/sci-fi/doctor-who-the-story-and-engine-ratings-newsupdate/)
*   [Share on twitter](https://twitter.com/intent/tweet?text=Doctor%20Who%20confirms%207-day%20ratings%20for%20The%20Story%20and%20the%20Engine%0A%0A&url=https://www.radiotimes.com/tv/sci-fi/doctor-who-the-story-and-engine-ratings-newsupdate/)
*   [Share on pinterest](https://www.pinterest.com/pin/create/button/?url=https://www.radiotimes.com/tv/sci-fi/doctor-who-the-story-and-engine-ratings-newsupdate/&media=https://images.immediate.co.uk/production/volatile/sites/3/2025/05/519192-1-84894ed-e1746713254820.jpg&description=Doctor%20Who%20confirms%207-day%20ratings%20for%20The%20Story%20and%20the%20Engine)
*   [Share on reddit](https://www.reddit.com/submit?url=https://www.radiotimes.com/tv/sci-fi/doctor-who-the-story-and-engine-ratings-newsupdate/&title=Doctor%20Who%20confirms%207-day%20ratings%20for%20The%20Story%20and%20the%20Engine)
*   [Email to a friend](mailto:?subject=On%20RadioTimes%20today:&body=I%20saw%20this%20and%20thought%20it%20might%20interest%20you...%0A%0Ahttps://www.radiotimes.com/tv/sci-fi/doctor-who-the-story-and-engine-ratings-newsupdate/)

The seven-day consolidated ratings for [Doctor Who](https://www.radiotimes.com/tv/sci-fi/doctor-who-season-15-release-date/) season 15 episode 5, The Story and the Engine, which saw the Doctor head to Lagos, Nigeria, and visit a barbershop with a secret, have been confirmed.

Ad

The episode, which aired at 7:10pm on BBC One on Saturday 10th May, [achieving an overnight audience of 1.59 million](https://www.radiotimes.com/tv/sci-fi/doctor-who-overnight-ratings-confirmed-story-engine-newsupdate/), saw a significant bump up to a consolidated figure of **2,704,000 viewers**across seven days, [as per Barb](https://www.barb.co.uk/viewing-data/most-viewed-programmes/).

That figure includes viewers from BBC One and BBC iPlayer – with episodes from the latest series of the beloved sci-fi show released on the on-demand platform at 8am on Saturdays ahead of their TV broadcast later that day.

The consolidated figure for The Story and the Engine is the lowest of any episode from Doctor Who season 15 so far.

3.571 million watched the series premiere, [The Robot Revolution](https://www.radiotimes.com/tv/sci-fi/doctor-who-robot-revolution-ratings-newsupdate/), 3.004 million watched the second episode, [Lux](https://www.radiotimes.com/tv/sci-fi/doctor-who-lux-7-day-ratings-newsupdate/), and 3.23 million viewers watched episode three, [The Well](https://www.radiotimes.com/tv/sci-fi/doctor-who-the-well-7-day-ratings-newsupdate/).

Episode 4, Lucky Day, originally returned the worst consolidated seven-day figures of the series with 2.802 million, but that has now been beaten by the fifth episode.

![Image 5: Ncuti Gatwa as the Doctor in Doctor Who episode The Story and the Engine. He's dressed in a stripey shirt and is holding the Vindicator tool.](https://images.immediate.co.uk/production/volatile/sites/3/2025/05/519191-0932c9d.jpg?quality=90&fit=700,467)

Ncuti Gatwa as the Doctor in Doctor Who episode The Story and the Engine.BBC Studios/Bad Wolf/Dan Fearon

The Story and the Engine, which saw The Doctor (Ncuti Gatwa) face off against the mysterious Barber (Ariyon Bakare), who used the magic of storytelling to aid his bid for revenge, was the 35th most-watched programme of the week overall, [according to Barb's figures](https://www.barb.co.uk/viewing-data/most-viewed-programmes/).

**Read more:**

*   [Doctor Who 'to return to BBC regardless of Disney involvement'](https://www.radiotimes.com/tv/sci-fi/doctor-who-bbc-future-newsupdate/)
*   [Doctor Who has a third epic villain incoming, Russell T Davies confirms](https://www.radiotimes.com/tv/sci-fi/doctor-who-unholy-trinity-third-villain-newsupdate/)

The latest episode, [The Interstellar Song Contest](https://www.radiotimes.com/tv/doctor-who-interstellar-song-contest-overnight-ratings-newsupdate/) which aired ahead of the Eurovision Song Contest on Saturday 17th May, returned an overnight audience of 2.57 million viewers – the highest of the season so far and was only beaten on the day by the FA Cup final and Eurovision itself.

The two-part finale of season 15 kicks off this weekend with Wish World, while the final episode, The Reality War, will not be getting an early release on BBC iPlayer and will be [simulcast around the world](https://www.radiotimes.com/tv/sci-fi/doctor-who-finale-schedule-iplayer-newsupdate/) at the same time as it is aired on BBC One.

Doctor Who's Lucky Day resolves one major series mystery
========================================================

Who sent the Doctor in search of Belinda?

![Image 5: Varada Sethu as Belinda Chandra and Ncuti Gatwa as The Doctor in Doctor Who](https://images.immediate.co.uk/production/volatile/sites/3/2025/04/518814-010e669.jpg?quality=90&resize=980,654)

Ad

There are a few significant mysteries at play in the new season of [Doctor Who](https://www.radiotimes.com/tv/sci-fi/doctor-who-season-15-release-date/) – but one big question posed this year has just been answered.

Season opener [The Robot Revolution](https://www.radiotimes.com/tv/sci-fi/doctor-who-the-robot-revolution/) saw the Doctor (Ncuti Gatwa) in search of nurse Belinda Chandra (Varada Sethu), giving chase from present-day Earth to an alien world when she was abducted by androids. [But why was he looking for her](https://www.radiotimes.com/tv/sci-fi/doctor-who-looking-for-belinda/)?

"I was told about you, by someone – it’s kind of a long story and I’ve got to be careful about timelines," the Doctor explained to Bel. "But he told me your name, that you would be important."

So, who told the Doctor about Belinda and tasked him with finding her?

Latest episode Lucky Day provides us with the reveal, opening with the Doctor's latest effort to get Belinda home as the pair arrive in London on New Year's Day 2007.

Here, they meet a young boy named Conrad Clark (Benjamin Chivers), whose brief interaction with the Doctor will end up having a profound impact.

![Image 6: Belinda Chandra (VARADA SETHU), The Doctor (NCUTI GATWA) & Young Conrad (BENJAMIN CHIVERS) in a dimly lit room](https://images.immediate.co.uk/production/volatile/sites/3/2025/04/518812-132a015.jpg?quality=90&fit=700,467)

Belind and the Doctor meet a young Conrad (Benjamin Chivers).BBC Studios/Bad Wolf/Lara Cornell

We meet Conrad again as an adult (now played by Jonah Hauer-King), and while he initially appears to be a sweet-natured, alien-obsessed podcaster – even pursuing a romance with Ruby Sunday (Millie Gibson) – he is eventually unmasked as a devious con man who uses his digital platforms to amplify dangerous conspiracy theories for financial gain.

Ruby is left heartbroken by Conrad's deception, leading the Doctor to confront the now-jailed villain. However, this is a Doctor from an earlier point in his personal timeline, shortly after [he and Ruby parted ways](https://www.radiotimes.com/tv/sci-fi/doctor-who-ruby-sunday-millie-gibson-exit-newsupdate/) and prior to his first meeting with Bel that we witnessed in The Robot Revolution.

"You betrayed my friend," the Time Lord seethes, but Conrad simply scoffs: "You've had plenty of friends. Have you met Belinda Chandra yet?"

![Image 7: Jonah Hauer-King as the adult Conrad Clark by the TARDIS](https://images.immediate.co.uk/production/volatile/sites/3/2025/04/518806-db76406.jpg?quality=90&fit=700,467)

Jonah Hauer-King as the adult Conrad Clark.

The Doctor doesn't know who Conrad is talking about and he refuses to elaborate, but the Doctor retorts with a few "spoilers" of his own, telling Conrad that he'll die aged just 49 of a heart attack, languishing in a prison cell "boiling in anger and poison".

"You aren’t even a figment, just ashes on the wind," he spits.

The episode ends with the Doctor having departed and the enigmatic Mrs Flood (Anita Dobson) arriving at Conrad's cell, [apparently to set him free](https://www.radiotimes.com/tv/sci-fi/doctor-who-lucky-day-ending-explained/) – so has her intervention changed his fate that the Doctor foresaw?

Whatever happens next, we now know that it was **Conrad Clark**who set the Doctor on the path to meeting Belinda.

That's far from all of this season's mysteries resolved, though. [Who is Mrs Flood](https://www.radiotimes.com/tv/sci-fi/doctor-who-mrs-flood-anita-dobson-explained/)? Why can't the Doctor return Belinda to Earth in 2025? And is it more than a coincidence that Belinda entered the Doctor's orbit after he'd previously met her descendant, [Mundy Flynn](https://www.radiotimes.com/tv/sci-fi/doctor-who-belinda-mundy-flynn-exclusive-newsupdate/)?

Four more episodes to go until we find out...

Doctor Who star reveals David Tennant nod in upcoming episode
=============================================================

"I was literally just like David Tennant."

By [Iona Rowan](https://www.digitalspy.com/author/240913/iona-rowan/ "Iona Rowan")Published: 29 April 2025

![Image 10: Play Icon](https://www.digitalspy.com/_assets/design-tokens/fre/static/icons/play.db7c035.svg?primary=%2523ffffff)![Image 11: david tennant, doctor who star beast](https://hips.hearstapps.com/hmg-prod/images/david-tennant-doctor-who-star-beast-657989ef18f8e.jpg?crop=1.00xw:0.846xh;0,0)

[Millie Gibson](https://www.digitalspy.com/tv/a60722447/doctor-who-millie-gibson-terrifying-scene-filming/) will be channelling some [David Tennant](https://www.digitalspy.com/tv/a64485931/itv-genius-game-david-tennant/) in her next _[Doctor Who](https://www.digitalspy.com/doctor-who/)_ appearance.

Next week's episode of the hit sci-fi show, titled 'Lucky Day', will mark the return of Gibson's Ruby Sunday after she last appeared in the 2024 Christmas special 'Joy to the World'.

Speaking to _[Radio Times](https://www.radiotimes.com/tv/sci-fi/doctor-who-lucky-day-connection-newsupdate/)_, the actor described her character's wardrobe in the new episode as "a bit more grown-up" but "still cool".

What to Read Next
-----------------

"She's kind of packed away the tweed vibes, I'd say," she continued, adding that one outfit reminded her of the style worn by David Tennant's Doctor.

"My favourite outfit is towards the end of the episode. I genuinely thought they dressed me like David Tennant!" she said.

![Image 12: millie gibson, ncuti gatwa, doctor who](https://hips.hearstapps.com/hmg-prod/images/millie-gibson-ncuti-gatwa-doctor-who-6641dcd24f0f1.jpg?resize=980:*)

James Pardon//BBC

**Related:**[**Best streaming services**](https://www.digitalspy.com/tech/best-tech-deals/g35899960/best-streaming-services/)

Advertisement - Continue Reading Below

"I had a pinstripe waistcoat and pinstripe pants and then a white shirt. I was literally just like David Tennant.

"Pam Downe, our costume designer, has a really subtle way of illustrating that these are what these characters would wear when they get older.

"The colour scheme is a lot of plums, a lot of dark greens and a lot of dark blues. It's just more mature colours."

![Image 13: david tennant, doctor who star beast](https://hips.hearstapps.com/hmg-prod/images/david-tennant-doctor-who-star-beast-657989ef18f8e.jpg?resize=980:*)

BBC

**Related: [David Tennant to guest present iconic BBC show](https://www.digitalspy.com/tv/a64568944/david-tennant-have-i-got-news-for-you/)**

The new episode will see Ruby face life back on earth without the Doctor. But when a dangerous new threat emerges, Ruby and UNIT must set out to save her new boyfriend Conrad (_[The Little Mermaid](https://www.digitalspy.com/little-mermaid/)_'s Jonah Hauer-King) from the terrifying Shreek.

[Previously speaking](https://www.digitalspy.com/tv/a61795821/doctor-who-season-15-jonah-hauer-king/) to [_Collider_](https://collider.com/doctor-who-ncuti-gatwa-millie-gibson-russell-t-davies/) about Ruby's journey in season 15, Gibson said: "It's the rare case where you see the companion after the Doctor.

"It's never been explored before, and I think it's such a beautiful and clever thing to do. Can you imagine traveling the world with The Doctor and then seeing how they cope with it after when your life just goes back to normal?

"It was the weirdest feeling. But yeah, I'm joined by the beautiful Jonah Hauer-King on her journey. He's a very, very interesting character, and he makes the show even more magical."

DOCTOR WHO is a British science-fiction drama series; in this episode, Ruby and the Doctor discover a baby farm is under threat from a malevolent creature.

threat and horror

There are sequences of moderate horror and fantasy threat in which a monster, known as the 'bogeyman', chases and terrorises characters including babies. additional issues

Content Advice

DOCTOR WHO is a British sci-fi adventure series; in this episode, Ruby and The Doctor travel to 1964 to see The Beatles at work, only to find music has vanished from the world - with catastrophic consequences.

threat and horror

A character emerges from a piano and restrains others using physical manifestations of musical notes; an elderly woman is heard screaming as it is implied she is killed off-screen. Frightened characters are dragged down corridors and bound by fantastical forces. A villainous character occasionally screams and shrieks in an intimidating manner and there are mild jump scares. We see a war-torn London in ruins, in a vision of a different reality which, it is implied, is the outcome of a nuclear conflict.

additional issues

There is brief verbal references to a character being 'hot'. A character suggests that another plays love songs for 'heartbroken lesbians', but there is no discriminatory intent behind this. There is mild bad language ('God', 'hell'). Scenes of very mild emotional upset include a character realising her loved ones have died in a post-apocalyptic alternate reality.

Content Advice

DOCTOR WHO is a British sci-fi adventure series; in this episode, after Ruby and The Doctor land on a war torn planet in the future, a deadly landmine threatens to bring their travels to an abrupt end.

violence

People are shot, vaporised and 'immolated' by futuristic guns and energy weapons. There are explosions and characters are shot by harpoon-like medical cables.

threat and horror

There are frequent, sustained sequences of threat and tension as characters find their lives at risk from a futuristic land mine device which is sensitive to movement; there are also scenes of gun threat and moments in which an AI-driven medical device threatens to kill its users.

injury detail

Characters are vaporised in blasts of energy which show their skeletal forms; dead bodies are compressed into small tubes of pink organic matter, with one of these showing an eyeball on its surface. Soldiers are seen with blood over their faces and, in one case, injured eyes.

additional issues

There is mild bad language ('fricking') and mild verbal sex references around a woman's mention of her hidden tattoo to a man she is attracted to. A character recalls visiting a 'lesbian gymkhana' in a comic moment. A young girl talks about the death of her mother and there are scenes of emotional upset around the loss of loved ones.

Content Advice

DOCTOR WHO is a British sci-fi adventure series; in this episode, Ruby finds herself stranded alone in the Welsh countryside, being followed by a mysterious woman.

threat and horror

There is a sense of building threat as an increasingly anxious woman is followed at a distance by a mysterious figure who never gets any closer or further away. At the climax of the episode the lights repeatedly go out, with the figure getting closer every time they come back on again; however, the outcome of this scene is not frightening. There is also a mild sequence of gun threat, which ends reassuringly. A preview for the next episode features mild fantasy threat as people are menaced by giant bug-like aliens.

additional issues

A woman jokes that her male friend would know about ‘fairy circles’, evoking an annoyed response from him. Another person criticises the perception that Welsh people are ‘witches and druids’ in touch with the supernatural, calling such stereotypes ‘racist’. Mild sex references occur when a man tells his girlfriend she seems distanced from him ‘even in bed’. In mild upsetting scenes, a woman emotionally rejects her adult daughter while under supernatural influence. Bad language includes ‘bloody’, ‘oh my God’, ‘hell’ and ‘bum’.

Content Advice

DOCTOR WHO is a British science-fiction series; in this episode, The Doctor and Ruby try to help a young woman living a heavily AI-assisted existence, escape from aliens intent on devouring her.

violence

A rogue flying droid punches through a man head, with brief suggestion of bloody detail. Humans are devoured by slug-like creatures, but this is depicted with minimal detail of injury, such as fantastical gunk or blood trailing behind a body, and a pair of legs partially visible amid a creature's tentacles. 

additional issues

A group of white characters refuse The Doctor's help for reasons that are implicitly to do with his race. They refer to The Doctor's powers as 'voodoo' and suggest they cannot travel with him because they have 'standards' to maintain, and for fear of being 'contaminated'. The Doctor offers to help them in spite of their prejudice, but appears visibly upset by their behaviour. Racism is clearly condemned by the main characters. There are brief sequences of fantastical threat in which humans are hunted, and then devoured, by large slug-like creatures with long tentacles. Rude humour comes in the form of comic dialogue about urinating. Bad language is very mild ('hell' and 'God'). Characters refer to others as 'hot' and 'tasty'.

5.content:
_****Alan Cumming Guest Stars as the Voice of Mr Ring-a-Ding in Second Episode****_
-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------

****Teaser Key Art and Character Image:****[****HERE****](https://press.disneyplus.com/media-kits/doctor-who)

Today, Disney Branded Television and the BBC jointly announced that season two of “[****Doctor Who****](https://www.disneyplus.com/series/doctor-who/1ml73V6phgyZ)” will premiere Saturday, April 12 (12:00 a.m. PDT / 3:00 a.m. EDT) on Disney+, where available, and exclusively on the BBC and BBC iPlayer in the UK. New episodes from the eight-part season will premiere weekly.

Emmy® Award winner ****Alan Cumming**** (“The Traitors”) will guest star in the second episode as Mr Ring-a-Ding, a happy, funny, singalong cartoon, who lives in Sunny Town with his friend Sunshine Sally. However, in 1952, after years of repeats in cinemas across the land, Mr Ring-a-Ding suddenly looks beyond the screen and sees the real world outside — and the consequences are terrifying. Cumming is returning to the Whoniverse after previously playing King James I in the 2018 episode “The Witchfinders.”

Showrunner, executive producer and writer Russell T Davies said, “Only Alan Cumming could give a runaway cartoon so much wit, malice, danger and fun. He makes the whole universe of ‘Doctor Who’ wilder and madder than ever, and it’s an absolute honour to welcome him on board the TARDIS.”

****Synopsis:**** The Doctor meets Belinda Chandra and begins an epic quest to get her back to Earth. But a mysterious force is stopping their return and the time-traveling TARDIS team must face great dangers, bigger enemies and wider terrors than ever before.

****Cast:****The new season stars Ncuti Gatwa as the Doctor, Varada Sethu as Belinda Chandra and Millie Gibson as Ruby Sunday. Previously announced guest cast includes Rose Ayling-Ellis, Christopher Chung, Anita Dobson, Michelle Greenidge, Jonah Hauer-King, Ruth Madeley, Jemma Redgrave and Susan Twist.

****Creative Team:****In addition to Davies, executive producers are Joel Collins, Phil Collinson, Julie Gardner and Jane Tranter.

****Production:****“Doctor Who” is produced by Bad Wolf, with BBC Studios for Disney Branded Television and BBC One and BBC iPlayer.

****SOCIAL MEDIA****

****Facebook****:[@DisneyPlus](https://www.facebook.com/DisneyPlus/)

****TikTok****:[@DisneyPlus](https://www.tiktok.com/@disneyplus)| [@DisneyDoctorWho](https://www.tiktok.com/@disneydoctorwho)

****Hashtag****: #DisneyPlus | #DoctorWho

Media Kit: [https://press.disneyplus.com/media-kits/doctor-who](https://press.disneyplus.com/media-kits/doctor-who)

****MEDIA CONTACTS****

****Disney Branded Television****

Steven Beydler

[Steven.J.Beydler@disney.com](mailto:Steven.J.Beydler@disney.com)

****BBC****

Joanna Allen

[Joanna.Allen@bbc.co.uk](mailto:Joanna.Allen@bbc.co.uk)

****BBC Studios****

Charlotte Clark

[Charlotte.Clark@bbc.com](mailto:Charlotte.Clark@bbc.com)

###

****ABOUT “DOCTOR WHO”****

Quintessentially British, Doctor Who is one of the longest running action-adventure television series in the world with legions of fans across the globe since it was launched by the BBC in 1963. Ncuti Gatwa took on the role of the Fifteenth Doctor in The Church On Ruby Road. Doctor Who remains one of the most watched programmes on iPlayer and was a top 5 series on Disney+ globally every week it aired, as well as being the BBC’s top drama for under 35’s this year making it one of the biggest programmes for the demographic across all streamers and broadcasters.

Doctor Who has a variety of licensees and partnerships spanning comics and collectibles, audiobooks, podcasts and magazines. Since 2012, over 17 million Sonic Screwdrivers and action figures, 19 million DVDs and over one million tickets for Doctor Who live events have sold globally. In 2023, BBC iPlayer launched the Whoniverse, a dedicated area where UK viewers can see more than 800 shows within the orbit of Doctor Who. Produced by Bad Wolf with BBC Studios for BBC and Disney Branded Television.

Doctor Who is available now on BBC iPlayer in the UK and on Disney+ in the rest of the world, where available. [www.doctorwho.tv](http://www.doctorwho.tv/)

****ABOUT DISNEY+****

Disney+ is the dedicated streaming home for movies and shows from Disney, Pixar, Marvel, Star Wars, and National Geographic, along with The Simpsons and much more. In select international markets, it also includes the general entertainment content brand, Star, and in the U.S., eligible bundle subscribers can also access extensive Hulu and ESPN+ content on Disney+, including next day TV, Hulu and ESPN Originals, live sports events and studio programming. The flagship direct-to-consumer streaming service from The Walt Disney Company, Disney+ offers an unmatched collection of exclusive originals, including feature-length films, documentaries, live-action and animated series, and short-form content. With unprecedented access to Disney’s long history of incredible film and television entertainment, Disney+ is also the exclusive streaming home for the newest releases from The Walt Disney Studios. Disney+ is available as a standalone streaming service or as part of bundle offerings in the U.S. that give subscribers access to different combinations of Disney+, Hulu, and ESPN+. For more, visit disneyplus.com, or find the Disney+ app on most mobile and connected TV devices.

****ABOUT DISNEY BRANDED TELEVISION****

Disney Branded Television encompasses the creative storytellers and production and content marketing teams responsible for Disney-branded television series, movies and other programming spanning live-action, animated and unscripted formats. The group fuels the Disney+ streaming platform and Disney Channel, Disney XD and Disney Jr. linear networks with content geared toward kids, tweens, teens and families, with stories that are imaginative, aspirational and reflective of their world and experiences.

****ABOUT BBC****

The BBC is the world’s leading public service broadcaster which is impartial and independent, and every day we create distinctive, world-class programmes and content which inform, educate and entertain millions of people in the UK and around the world. The BBC includes a portfolio of television services, national and local radio networks, and global digital services.

****ABOUT BBC STUDIOS****

BBC Studios is a commercial subsidiary of the BBC Group with sales of £2.1 billion (2021/22: £1,630 million). Able to take an idea seamlessly from thought to screen and beyond, the business is built on two operating areas: the global Content Studio, which produces, invests and distributes content globally and Channels & Streaming, with BBC branded channels, services and joint ventures in the UK and internationally. Around 2,500 hours of award-winning British programmes are made by the business every year, with over 80% of total BBC Studios revenues coming from non-BBC customers including Discovery, Apple and Netflix. Its content is internationally recognised across a broad range of genres and specialisms, with brands like Strictly Come Dancing/Dancing with the Stars, Top Gear, the Planet series, Bluey and Doctor Who. BBC.com is BBC Studios’ global digital news platform, offering up-to-the-minute international news, in-depth analysis and features.

17.title: Pete McTighe on writing for 'The War Between the Land and the Sea' | Doctor Who
17.description: The 'Lucky Day' writer speaks to Doctor Who Magazine about coming aboard for the next adventure in the Whoniverse.
17.content:
Products

December 01, 2025

The _Lucky Day_ writer speaks to Doctor Who Magazine about coming aboard for the next adventure in the Whoniverse.

[_The War Between the Land and the Sea_](https://www.doctorwho.tv/shows/the-war-between-the-land-and-the-sea)debuts this week on BBC One and BBC iPlayer in the UK, following on Disney+ for the rest of the world in 2026. Joining showrunner Russell T Davies as co-writer is [_Lucky Day_](https://www.doctorwho.tv/stories/lucky-day)writer Pete McTighe, also known to Doctor Who fans for his work on _Tales of the TARDIS_ and a series of extra-Whoniversal announcement trailers for the Collection Blu-ray series.

**Doctor Who Magazine** spoke to Pete about what to expect in the exciting new spin-off series, as well as his experience joining the writing team. Read an exclusive preview of the interview from the latest issue below...

**Doctor Who Magazine issue 624 is on sale from Thursday 6th November. You can order it**[**here.**](https://bbc.in/DWMSub)

![Image 1: TWB](https://cms.doctorwho.tv/sites/default/files/2025-12/dwtv-gallery-module-watermark-template-382367b4a9.jpg)

**Co-writer and executive producer Pete McTighe on**_**The War Between the Land and the Sea**_**…**

“I’ve been working on _The War Between_ since 2023. After I handed in my first draft of _Lucky Day_, my episode for Season 2 of Doctor Who, Russell called me in for a meeting and gave me Episode 1 that he’d already written. He said, ‘I’d love you to come on board and write some more episodes with me.’ I was thrilled because I loved Episode 1 and to work more with Russell is a dream – we work really well together. It’s been really exciting, crafting it all with him, and then seeing the team put it all together.

“Malcolm Hulke did such a fantastic job in creating the [Silurians](https://www.doctorwho.tv/characters/silurians) and the [Sea Devils](https://www.doctorwho.tv/characters/sea-devils). It’s a great idea, a way of doing an alien invasion story without them being alien – he was a very clever man and his stories stand the test of time. Because I knew the history, I was able to bring in a few little Easter eggs for fans of the classic series. The footage we’ve recorded for this series looks fantastic – this has been the best job of my career so far.”

![Image 2: DWM 624](https://cms.doctorwho.tv/sites/default/files/2025-12/dwm624-outer-bag-08405219b9.jpg)

#### Included with this issue:

_**THE WAR BETWEEN THE LAND AND THE SEA**_**COLLECTOR’S ART CARDS AND AN AUDIO ADVENTURE WITH THE**[**NINTH DOCTOR**](https://www.doctorwho.tv/characters/ninth-doctor)

#### In the magazine:

*   As _THE WAR BETWEEN THE LAND AND THE SEA_ surfaces on BBC One and iPlayer, we speak to star **RUSSELL TOVEY** about his role as [Barclay Pierre-Dupont](https://www.doctorwho.tv/characters/barclay).

*   Writer **PETE McTIGHE**, producer **JOEL COLLINS** and director **DYLAN HOLMES WILLIAMS** discuss the development of this eagerly awaited spin-off.

*   A preview of the new 90-minute version of [Third Doctor](https://www.doctorwho.tv/characters/third-doctor) classic [_**THE SEA DEVILS**_](https://www.doctorwho.tv/stories/the-sea-devils).

*   UNIT intelligence on previous **SEA DEVIL** skirmishes!

*   Back to 1968! UNIT’s first encounter with the Doctor – 57 years ago!

*   Concept artist **PETER McKINSTRY** talks about his work and his new book _The Art of Time Travel_.

*   Doctor Who showrunner **RUSSELL T DAVIES** shares his latest 12 Days of Christmas!

*   Looking back on 60 years of the Doctor Who Annual.

*   We remember Doctor Who’s very first [Dalek](https://www.doctorwho.tv/characters/daleks) December…

*   …and the many ways in which Charles Dickens’ _A Christmas Carol_ has influenced Doctor Who.

*   We excavate the Cave-Monsters – in the first part of our deep dive into the fact and fiction of [_Doctor Who and the Silurians_](https://www.doctorwho.tv/stories/the-silurians).

*   A ghost story for Christmas featuring the[Fifteenth Doctor](https://www.doctorwho.tv/characters/fifteenth-doctor)…

#### Regular features:

*   **GALLIFREY GUARDIAN:**News including the launch of _The War Between the Land and the Sea_, a round-up of this year’s Doctor Who Day activity, and a Children in Need Special.

*   **Reviews** – featuring the latest audios, books and action figures.

*   **Other Worlds** – the essential guide to new stories in Doctor Who’s expanded universe – including the War Doctor’s clash with every [Cyberman](https://www.doctorwho.tv/characters/cybermen) ever!

*   **Prizes to be won** – you could win a massive Christmas bundle of Blu-rays and CDs!

**Doctor Who Magazine issue 624 is on sale from Thursday 6th November. You can order it**[**here.**](https://bbc.in/DWMSub)

Doctor Who: Lucky Day – season two episode four recap
=====================================================

This article is more than 7 months old

Millie Gibson returns as Ruby Sunday to take centre-stage in a battle with internet conspiracy theorists. No one could accuse this show of not being timely

[Martin Belam](https://www.theguardian.com/profile/martin-belam)

Sat 3 May 2025 19.55 BSTLast modified on Sun 4 May 2025 16.13 BST

[Share](mailto:?subject=DoctorWho:LuckyDay%E2%80%93seasontwoepisodefourrecap&body=https://www.theguardian.com/tv-and-radio/2025/may/03/doctor-who-lucky-day-ncuti-gatwa-varada-sethu-millie-gibson-recap?CMP=share_btn_url)

In a series of Doctor Who with only eight episodes, having a Doctor-lite episode feels something of a luxury. This greatest hits remix of previous episodes like [Love and Monsters](https://tardis.wiki/wiki/Love_%26_Monsters_/(TV_story/)), [Blink](https://tardis.wiki/wiki/Blink_/(TV_story/)) and [Turn Left](https://tardis.wiki/wiki/Turn_Left_/(TV_story/)), where we only see glimpses of the Doctor in the background, just about earned its place in the run.

Much of the weight of the episode was carried by whether you could invest in hate-watching Jonah Hauer-King as odious grifter Conrad Clark, the podcast host and conspiracy theory propagandist who had gone through what he called the “chore” of getting to know Ruby Sunday (Millie Gibson) in order to “expose the lies” of Unit.

Having already watched Ruby live out a post-Doctor life in a different timeline in [73 Yards](https://www.theguardian.com/tv-and-radio/article/2024/may/25/doctor-who-73-yards-millie-gibson-ncuti-gatwa-wales-witchcraft-folk-horror-recap), there was a real risk of a re-tread, as this episode hit several similar beats, including her aimlessness and romantic failures, and being trapped in a pub in a small village with a menace outside. But Gibson got the best line. Asked who put her in charge, her delivery of “or go and get some fresh air, big man, and see what happens” was deliciously waspish.

Pete McTighe had previously written the muddled messaging of [Kerblam!](https://www.theguardian.com/tv-and-radio/2018/nov/18/doctor-who-recap-series-37-episode-7-kerblam) for the 13th Doctor, and did a better job here of targeting the conspiracy sphere than he did targeting Amazon in that. The tension ratcheted up sharply once Unit were on the scene, and Jemma Redgrave (Kate Lethbridge-Stewart) was put in a position where she ceased knowing where to draw the line.

![Image 3: Kate Lethbridge Stewart (Jemma Redgrave) and Colonel Ibrahim (Alexander Devrient).](https://i.guim.co.uk/img/media/a94bbb040ff57ef13c90bae9dbf74b46389c4912/0_0_4800_3200/master/4800.jpg?width=445&dpr=1&s=none&crop=none)[View image in fullscreen](https://www.theguardian.com/tv-and-radio/2025/may/03/doctor-who-lucky-day-ncuti-gatwa-varada-sethu-millie-gibson-recap#img-2)

Ratchet that tension! … Kate Lethbridge-Stewart (Jemma Redgrave) and Colonel Ibrahim (Alexander Devrient). Photograph: BBC Studios/Bad Wolf/James Pardon

The episode touched upon modern phenomena with the doxing of Unit staff, the livestreaming of the armed standoff via body cam and the mainstreaming of conspiracy theories on broadcast legacy media. And if you thought the idea of Think Tank seemed far-fetched, just recall the moment in 2021 when [anti-vaccine campaigners filmed themselves “serving legal papers”](https://www.itv.com/news/anglia/2021-10-21/anti-vax-campaigners-serve-legal-papers-on-hospital) to hospital staff alleging “crimes against humanity” at the height of the Covid pandemic.

**Sum it up in one sentence?**
------------------------------

What if [Doctor Who](https://www.theguardian.com/tv-and-radio/doctor-who) did another episode like Love and Monsters, but without the terrible ending.

**Life** **aboard the Tardis**
------------------------------

We only got three Tardis moments, with Belinda (Varada Sethu) and the Doctor (Ncuti Gatwa) using the vortex indicator in 2007, Ruby and the Doctor having their own encounter with the Shreek – dialogue indicated that happened directly after last year’s [The Devil’s Chord](https://www.theguardian.com/tv-and-radio/article/2024/may/11/doctor-who-space-babies-devils-chord-ncuti-gatwa-millie-gibson-beatles-jinkx-monsoon) – and the Doctor telling off Clark in the Tardis at some unspecified point between the two.

**F****ear factor**
-------------------

![Image 4: Conrad (Jonah Hauer-King) talks into a large microphone.](https://i.guim.co.uk/img/media/0f9e56ee404f70b52b0a00e08fcde56da57dea51/0_0_4800_3200/master/4800.jpg?width=445&dpr=1&s=none&crop=none)[View image in fullscreen](https://www.theguardian.com/tv-and-radio/2025/may/03/doctor-who-lucky-day-ncuti-gatwa-varada-sethu-millie-gibson-recap#img-3)

All the monsters are human … odious grifter Conrad (Jonah Hauer-King). Photograph: BBC Studios/Bad Wolf/James Pardon

Someone who was definitely feeling the fear factor was [the Vlinx](https://www.doctorwho.tv/characters/the-vlinx), who hilariously couldn’t abandon its post on the Unit bridge fast enough. The Shreek were monster of the week, and, rather like the Dregs in [Orphan 55](https://www.theguardian.com/tv-and-radio/2020/jan/12/doctor-who-recap-series-38-episode-three-orphan-55), worked better in the shadows and in brief shots than out in the open. The reveal that, at least at one point, they actually _were_ just men in hoax rubber suits felt like yet more meta-commentary on the production of the show. But all the real monsters in this episode were human.

**Mysteries and questions**
---------------------------

Surely “the guv’nor” is not going to turn out to be the recurring Anita Dobson’s villain character name?

**Deeper into the vortex**
--------------------------

![Image 5: Shirley (Ruth Madeley).](https://i.guim.co.uk/img/media/2ddfdcc60293b59bb82d40e5c61ec10f582b291d/0_0_4800_3200/master/4800.jpg?width=445&dpr=1&s=none&crop=none)[View image in fullscreen](https://www.theguardian.com/tv-and-radio/2025/may/03/doctor-who-lucky-day-ncuti-gatwa-varada-sethu-millie-gibson-recap#img-4)

She’ll be back … expect more from Shirley (Ruth Madeley) soon. Photograph: BBC Studios/Bad Wolf/James Pardon

*   It was good to see the London Eye being used as a tourist attraction again on New Year’s Eve in 2007. Public confidence must have recovered after it was discovered to be the Auton transmitter in [Rose](https://tardis.wiki/wiki/Rose_/(TV_story/)), set in March 2005.
    
*   The first time we saw the Doctor operate the Tardis with a snap of his fingers was in 2008 episode [Forest of the Dead](https://tardis.wiki/wiki/Forest_of_the_Dead_/(TV_story/)), when David Tennant’s 10th Doctor tries it after having been told by River Song that her Doctor in the future could open the doors that way.
    
*   Among the aliens Clark lists as Unit hoaxes are the Sycorax, who appeared in David Tennant’s debut [The Christmas Invasion](https://tardis.wiki/wiki/The_Christmas_Invasion_/(TV_story/)), and “yetis in the underground”, a reference to the partially missing 1968 Patrick Troughton story [The Web of Fear](https://tardis.wiki/wiki/The_Web_of_Fear_/(TV_story/)), which first introduced us to the character of Kate’s dad, who then had the rank of Col Lethbridge-Stewart.
    
*   We can expect to see Unit again later in the year, as Redgrave, Alexander Devrient and Ruth Madeley are all reprising their roles in spin-off The War Between the Land and the Sea.
    
*   This is the second time in a fortnight that a main character has been told their name is “ridiculous”, as Clark used the word to belittle Ruby after we’d seen Belinda dismiss the Doctor’s chosen moniker during [Lux](https://www.theguardian.com/tv-and-radio/2025/apr/19/doctor-who-lux-ncuti-gatwa-varada-sethu-alan-cumming-recap) the same way.
    
*   [Think Tank](https://tardis.wiki/wiki/National_Institute_for_Advanced_Scientific_Research) was the name of the scientific institute developing a giant robot and infiltrated by conspiracy-minded scientists during Tom Baker’s 1974 debut [Robot](https://tardis.wiki/wiki/Robot_/(TV_story/)).
    
*   If you missed it, earlier this week we pondered [whether the whole enterprise might be on its last legs](https://www.theguardian.com/tv-and-radio/2025/apr/30/is-doctor-who-doomed-ncuti-gatwa-russell-t-davies) …
    

**Next time**
-------------

Lagos! A huge spider! The Story and the Engine is the episode that, during the Q&A section at the premiere event for [The Robot Revolution](https://www.theguardian.com/tv-and-radio/2025/apr/12/doctor-who-robot-revolution-ncuti-gatwa-varada-sethu-recap), Gatwa said he was most looking forward to people seeing. See you then!
